subject.title: chore(deps): bump the actions group across 1 directory with 14 updates

question: Does the CI/security owner approve advancing the pinned revisions of `actions/create-github-app-token`, Docker actions, `actions/stale`, CodeQL, attestation, and `openai/codex-action` in credential-bearing OpenClaw workflows?
rationale: The patch is mechanically generated, but it changes executable third-party code at the repository’s credential and publishing boundaries; that acceptance decision cannot be inferred from Dependabot metadata or routine CI alone.

options.title: Approve after upstream review
options.body: Review the upstream release diffs and action manifests for the credential-bearing revisions, then approve this exact head if their permission and secret-handling contracts remain acceptable.

options.title: Split sensitive action families
options.body: Keep low-risk setup-action bumps separate and send token, Docker publish, CodeQL, stale, attestation, and Codex-action revisions through a focused security review.

options.title: Hold the update
options.body: Leave the current pins in place until a CI/security owner can verify the changed action code and release notes.

recommendation.title: Approve after upstream review
recommendation.body: Review the upstream release diffs and action manifests for the credential-bearing revisions, then approve this exact head if their permission and secret-handling contracts remain acceptable.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent activity on the affected release and Codex-agent workflow paths makes steipete the strongest available routing candidate.
